correctness.rationale: For n>=5 the antipodal quotient is triangle-free with exactly two common neighbors per distance-two pair. Every connected three-set lies in one square tetrahedron in the dual; no five-faces exist by Mantel counting. Exactly two legitimate free-face collapses per square leave the cubical two-skeleton of RP^(n-1) and b_n unattached triangle-free edges. Fundamental group Z/2, free H2 rank h_n by Euler, integral UCT and combinatorial Alexander duality yield the complete two-degree formula. The local face and boundary computations replay for n=5,6,7; finite-field checks are not substituted for the integral proof.

value.rationale: The source is a natural infinite family of vertex-transitive projective cube graphs, not an arbitrary small slice. Uniform integer Z/2 torsion in pure, very high-dimensional ordinary cut complexes is a structurally motivated obstruction to shellability, with explicit free ranks in two adjacent degrees. The projective-space origin explains the torsion and distinguishes folded cubes from unfolded hypercubes; the all-dimensions result includes both parity classes and a canonical Clebsch case.
